content.text:
I submitted index 22 (Sb 0.45, Y 0.55), which had the highest efficiency (EQE) of the three compositions I measured: 0.101%. All three merit measurements are used.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 28 | 0.63 | 0.081 |
| 24 | 0.52 | 0.089 |
| 22 | 0.45 | 0.101 |

- **Why I looked at the Sb-rich half:** the model predictions put every stable Sb–Y oxide's band gap above the 2.1 eV light energy. Of these, YSbO4 (Sb 0.5) has the lowest predicted gap at about 3.0 eV and is predicted stable. On the Y-rich side, Y3SbO7 is predicted at 3.6 eV, so it should absorb even less.
- **Trend:** EQE went up at every step as Sb went down, so it hadn't levelled off when the budget ran out. The best composition may lie at even lower Sb, around indices 19–21, near where the model fitted to the measurements (GP) suggested looking next (index 20).
- **Main gap:** nothing below Sb 0.45 was measured, including the whole Y-rich half. Ruling that side out rests only on the predicted wide band gaps.
- **XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are actually present is unconfirmed.

All EQE values are very low (about 0.1%), which fits light at 2.1 eV sitting below the band gaps of every phase checked.
